title: Gyeran Bap
subtitle: Egg rice with sesame and soy sauce
excerpt: Hot cooked rice is topped with a fried egg, a drizzle of soy sauce and sesame oil, a scatter of sesame seeds and sliced spring onion, then mixed together at the table until everything combines into a savoury, glossy bowl. This serves 1 and takes 7 minutes. It is the Korean answer to having almost nothing in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Gyeran bap is the kind of dish that does not appear in cookbooks because it barely needs a recipe. Korean households have eaten egg on rice as a fallback meal for generations. The dish reflects the centrality of bap, cooked rice, in Korean daily eating, and the way a few basic pantry ingredients can turn it into a satisfying meal in minutes.

content.text: Gyeran bap takes about 7 minutes and serves 1. It is a bowl of hot rice with a fried or raw egg on top, seasoned with soy sauce, sesame oil, and butter. The egg yolk mixes into the rice as you eat. Use fresh hot rice so the yolk cooks from the heat of the bowl.

Use the smallest pan you have for the egg and fry it in the lightest film of oil over a moderate heat. The white should be just set at the edges and still slightly translucent in the centre when it goes on the rice. It will finish cooking from the heat of the bowl. A lacy white from high-heat frying in a lot of oil is not what you are after here.
Spoon the hot cooked rice into a bowl. If using butter, place a small knob on top of the rice now and let it melt.
Heat the neutral oil in a small frying pan over a moderate heat. Crack in the eggs and fry until the whites are just set but the yolks remain runny, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Slide the fried eggs on top of the rice.
Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil over the egg and rice. Scatter over the spring onion and sesame seeds.
Break the yolk and mix everything together with a spoon until the rice is coated in the egg and seasoning. Eat immediately.

items.symptom: Rice and egg feel dry and do not come together when mixed
items.cause: The rice was cold or dry, or the soy sauce and sesame oil quantities were too small
items.fix: The rice must be hot. If using leftover rice, reheat it with a splash of water in a covered bowl in the microwave until steaming. Add a little more soy sauce or sesame oil if needed.

items.symptom: Yolk broke during frying and cooked through
items.cause: The heat was too high or the eggs were not handled gently when cracked
items.fix: Crack each egg into a small cup first, then slide it gently into the pan. Keep the heat at medium rather than high. Remove the pan from the heat a little early if the yolk is about to set.

items.cause: Too much soy sauce was added, or the rice was already seasoned
items.fix: Start with half a tablespoon of soy sauce and add more to taste. Unseasoned short-grain rice has a natural sweetness that balances well with a moderate amount of soy.

content.text: Gyeran bap is what many Koreans eat when they are alone, in a hurry, or have very little in the fridge. It is not a restaurant dish and it is not a dish for showing off. It is simply a very good way to eat rice and eggs together. Korean university students eat it constantly. Korean adults eat it on a Monday morning when nothing else is prepared. The optional butter is a more recent addition that some people swear by.
